author.headline: Senior Vice President - Regulatory Affairs at Darena Solutions

comments.text:
Josh,
Welcome to the wonderful world of MIPS and value-based care, where nothing is ever quite as simple as it first appears! Really nice framework for making a complicated set of ACO reporting choices easier to understand. One thing I would add is the operational reality that for many ACOs, the real challenge is consistently aggregating complete, measure-ready data across multiple EHRs and participant TINs. In practice, data completeness and interoperability can influence the reporting choice just as much as the scoring methodology. Great perspective and a great way to frame the discussion.

author.name: Mark Oswald
author.headline: Experienced Data and AI Architect. I’m passionate about using Data and AI to solve problems, create opportunities, and innovate within the Healthcare and Life Sciences industries.

comments.text:
Welcome to the World of VBC and it's interesting collection of problems/solutions.

Given your interest in simulation, you might be interested in looking at Vantage - https://github.com/mark64oswald/vantage-docs.

Vantage is a simulation tool that can generate populations that mirror your own, and then model four interconnected outcome domains:
◾ Risk Adjustment (V24/V28 scoring, RAF impact)
◾ Stars & Quality (competitive scoring with dynamic cut-points)
◾ Medical Cost / MLR (integrated P&L projections)
◾ RADV Audit Exposure (the liability side most platforms ignore)

From there, you can manipulate a set of six connected intervention levers — care management, coding initiatives, formulary design, PA policy, provider contracts, benefit design — and show how each change ripples across every domain simultaneously.

If you read through the public documentation and would like to explore deeper or collaborate, I'd be happy to make the rest of it public.

comments.text: A simulator earns its keep only if it's pinned to the spec version the payer will audit against, not the one currently published. Reporting year logic versus audit year logic is where the reconciliation surprises live. Can it replay a measurement year under the spec as it stood mid year, before a revision changed denominator eligibility?
